issues.legal_issue: Scattered structures on a small fraction of a large area do not, by themselves, prevent use of the urgency power to dispense with an acquisition inquiry.
material_facts: A large area was acquired for planned housing development.
Houses, huts, cattle sheds, and similar structures were located only on a fraction of the area.
The acquisition authority invoked the urgency power and dispensed with the inquiry into objections.
issues.conclusion: The existence of a few structures on a small fraction of the large area did not invalidate the use of the urgency power.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 17(1) and 17(4) of the Rajasthan Land Acquisition Act, 1953, whether land is waste or arable is assessed by its general nature and condition. Applying State of U.P. v. Smt. Pista Devi, scattered superstructures do not prevent use of the urgency power for a large-area acquisition; Sarju Prasad Saha v. State of Uttar Pradesh concerned the converse situation, in which most of the land was built upon, and does not govern this one.

predicates.large_area_acquisition: The government proposed to acquire a large area of land.
predicates.structures_confined_to_small_fraction: The landowners had structures on only a small fraction of the area proposed for acquisition.
predicates.urgency_inquiry_waiver_invoked: The government invoked an urgency power to dispense with the usual inquiry into objections.

issues.definition: When a large-area acquisition uses an urgency waiver and structures occupy only a small fraction of the area, those scattered structures do not invalidate the waiver.

issues.legal_issue: An acquisition notification invoking the urgency power need not expressly state that the land is waste or arable.
material_facts: The acquisition notifications did not recite that the land was waste or arable.
The challenge asserted that the absence of that recital invalidated the notifications.
issues.conclusion: The omission of a recital that the land was waste or arable did not invalidate the notification.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17(4) of the Rajasthan Land Acquisition Act, 1953 does not require the notification itself to recite that the land is waste or arable. Dora Phalauli v. State of Punjab was distinguished because its reasoning also concerned the absence of a statement that the government considered the urgency power applicable.

predicates.urgency_acquisition_proceeding: The government issued an acquisition notification invoking an urgency procedure that dispenses with an inquiry into objections.
predicates.notification_omits_land_condition_recita: The notification did not state that the land was waste or arable.

issues.definition: In an urgency acquisition proceeding, omitting a statement about the land's condition does not invalidate the notification.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not overturn the government's subjective urgency satisfaction when material fairly supports it, by reassessing that material as an appellate authority.
material_facts: The government found an acute shortage of land and substantial housing demand.
The housing authority had obtained funding under a time-bound programme and needed to use it by a specified deadline.
The authority had engaged staff for the project, and delay from an objection inquiry could endanger the programme and schedule.
The government formed the view that immediate possession was necessary, and the court found material capable of fairly supporting that view.
issues.conclusion: The court upheld the government's urgency satisfaction and would not re-examine the supporting material as an appellate authority.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 5(A) and 17(4) of the Rajasthan Land Acquisition Act, 1953, the urgency satisfaction is subjective. If material exists on which the government could fairly form that satisfaction, a reviewing court does not interfere by evaluating the material as an appellate authority. The court relied on State of U.P. v. Smt. Pista Devi and stated that the principle also applies generally to subjective satisfaction.

predicates.urgency_inquiry_waiver_proceeding: The government used an urgency procedure to dispense with an inquiry into objections in an acquisition proceeding.
predicates.government_formed_urgency_satisfaction: The government concluded that the circumstances required urgent acquisition action.
predicates.material_fairly_supports_urgency: The record contained material capable of fairly supporting the government's conclusion, such as pressing public need and a time-sensitive project threatened by delay.

issues.definition: In an acquisition proceeding using an urgency waiver, a supported government urgency conclusion is not overturned by a court merely by reassessing the material as an appellate authority.

issues.legal_issue: The government cannot withdraw from an acquisition after possession of the land has been taken.
material_facts: The government had taken possession of the acquired land and delivered it to the housing authority.
A later communication about releasing the land contemplated restoring possession and accounting for development costs.
issues.conclusion: Withdrawal from the acquisition was unavailable because possession had already been taken.
issues.legal_principle: Section 48 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 does not permit withdrawal from an acquisition once possession of the land has been taken.

predicates.withdrawal_from_acquisition_claimed: A party claimed that the government had withdrawn from an acquisition.
predicates.possession_taken_by_acquiring_authority: The government or acquiring authority had taken possession of the acquired land.

issues.definition: When withdrawal from an acquisition is claimed after the acquiring authority has taken possession, withdrawal is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: A tentative governmental decision to release acquired land does not constitute a final decision to withdraw from the acquisition.
material_facts: A minister recommended releasing land, and the recommendation received approval from the head of government.
Before the proposed release was implemented, the government sought information about development works, expenditure, and possession so that the authority could be dealt with before land was returned.
The proposed release was not implemented, and the government later reversed course.
issues.conclusion: There had been no final decision to release the land; a tentative decision was insufficient to establish withdrawal from the acquisition.
issues.legal_principle: For a governmental decision to effect withdrawal from an acquisition, the decision must be final rather than provisional or tentative. The court found it unnecessary to decide whether the tentative decision had been communicated.

predicates.withdrawal_from_acquisition_claimed: A party claimed that the government had withdrawn from an acquisition.
predicates.release_decision_tentative: The government's decision to release the land remained provisional rather than final.
predicates.implementation_steps_remained_pending: Further governmental steps, such as obtaining information needed before returning the land, remained outstanding.

issues.definition: A claimed withdrawal is not effected when the proposed release remains tentative and steps to implement it are still pending.
